Area.evidence_source: Respondents experienced that different aspects of care alleviated their feelings of shame. For many respondents, being treated with kindness and respect during the first encounters at the hospital alleviated their initial shame reaction after the suicide attempt and helped them make the decision to agree to being admitted into the psychiatric clinic. Respondents described that their feelings of shame were exacerbated when they felt that they had exposed themselves too much and when they experienced the personnel as unsympathetic, disrespectful, authoritative, and punishing.
